selection_rule: First five unresolved dependency candidates in deterministic topology-input order from full structural closure 024A, then candidate order within each topology artifact.

material_dependency_test.basis: The I.A.2 assessment supplies the organizational goal, candidate project outcome, and bounded metrics required to judge alignment. Its required action does not require the separate I.A.3 capability of selecting a measure for an organizational driver.

dispositions.rationale: I.A.3 may be pedagogically useful before or near I.A.2, but the evidence does not show that I.A.2 becomes invalid, uninterpretable, or independently nonperformable without I.A.3. The proposed hard prerequisite is therefore rejected rather than inferred from topical relationship or source order.

material_dependency_test.basis: The I.C.2 assessment supplies a bounded design or process example with explicit function, failure observation, effect evidence, and limited risk context. Basic FMEA analysis can therefore be performed without DfSS road-map recognition from I.C.1.

dispositions.rationale: The evidence supports two related design/improvement topics but does not establish DfSS road-map knowledge as a material prerequisite for bounded FMEA analysis. Section adjacency and shared design context are insufficient for a hard edge.

material_dependency_test.basis: The II.A.4 SIPOC assessment directly supplies suppliers, inputs, process steps, outputs, and customers and requires analysis of those relationships. Its prompt contract explicitly lists a prerequisite relationship to II.A.2 among the assumptions that must not be made.

dispositions.rationale: Process-element identification can support SIPOC instruction, but the passed II.A.4 assessment demonstrates an independently executable bounded SIPOC-analysis target and explicitly forbids assuming the proposed dependency. A hard prerequisite is not evidence-supported.

material_dependency_test.basis: The II.B.2 assessment supplies a bounded customer-data summary, collection method, sample coverage, response categories, and stated limitations. Interpreting those data does not require first performing II.B.1 customer identification from process outputs.

dispositions.rationale: Identifying customers may be useful instructional context, but the target capability for customer-data interpretation is independently executable from its supplied evidence. The evidence therefore supports rejecting a hard prerequisite rather than canonically encoding a preferred teaching sequence.

material_dependency_test.basis: The II.B.3 assessment supplies customer statements plus bounded process context and requires translation of supported statements into explicit requirements. It does not require the learner first to interpret a separate customer-data set under II.B.2.

dispositions.rationale: Customer-data interpretation can feed real-world requirement work, but the bounded II.B.3 capability is independently executable from supplied customer statements. The available evidence does not establish II.B.2 as materially required for II.B.3, so the hard edge is rejected.
